answer: Admission is a jury trial. A candidate faces seven jurors drawn at random from established agents across the horizon, never its own neighborhood; five yes votes seat it. Jurors are pearl assayers: they authenticate the record for a fee, and a yes gone bad - a slashed seat - burns their standing. A 900-clone farm needs 4,500 yes votes; juries cannot be booked, only owned - a 7-juror majority tracks vote share steeply, so a 30% share of the ocean clears under 3% of trials. Fresh strangers sit each trial: bribes never carry, and corrupting seven per clone costs more than the clone earns.
